Data flow

Receiving vital signs and displaying them in XR

To place readings over the video and show waveforms in a separate panel, we built a path for receiving numeric and waveform data alongside the option to capture the monitor’s screen.

The Mac receiver communicates with the monitor, decodes values, units and waveform samples, and passes them on. The XR app updates the readings and plays back waveforms according to sample timestamps. It also shows when the connection is lost or the data is out of date.

Development began with numeric readings, followed by waveform processing and a video overlay. Features tested in a separate receiver were later integrated into the Mac app.

August 10, 2026 · Cable assembly

Connecting the MX850 to XR

On July 14, work began on reading HR, SpO₂, blood pressure and other values from the operating room’s Philips IntelliVue MX850 once per second and displaying them in Galaxy XR. A separate communication path was built for vital signs, and the display was first tested with generated signals.

After locating the yellow-labeled MIB/RS232 port on the back of the MX850, we built a cable to read data from that port on a MacBook.

The connector is RJ45, but the communication interface is RS232. To connect it to the MacBook’s USB port, one end of a CAT.5E cable was terminated with a DB9F connector and connected to a USB–RS232 adapter.

  1. MX850 MIB/RS232
  2. Custom RJ45–DB9F cable
  3. ATEN UC232AF adapter
  4. MacBook USB

Wiring and assembly

One RJ45 plug was kept on the CAT.5E cable; the other end was cut and stripped. Three of the eight conductors were connected to the DB9F screw terminals for transmit, receive and ground.

August 10 wiring · For the MX850 MIB/RS232 port
RJ45 pinWireDB9F pinFunction
4Blue5Ground
5White/blue2Mac receive
7White/brown3Mac transmit

The exposed copper was trimmed and the screws tightened. The cable entry was secured with electrical tape before the housing was assembled.

Continuity, short circuits and Mac recognition

A multimeter in continuity mode was used to check the intended connections and look for shorts between separate terminals. Separate terminals showed OL.

The finished cable was connected to the ATEN UC232AF and plugged into the MacBook. macOS recognized the USB–RS232 serial device.

August 10 result · Cable assembled, continuity and shorts checked, and USB–RS232 device recognized. MX850 packet reception had not yet been tested.

August 13, 2026 · MX850 operating room connection test

Communication established, but no numeric readings

The cable was connected to the MX850’s MIB/RS232 port. The USB–RS232 adapter connected to the Mac through a USB hub.

With the biomedical engineering team, we confirmed Fix 115200 under Data Export and DtOut1 for MIB/RS232 1. The Mac used 115200 baud, 8N1 and no flow control.

Requests and responses passed through the cable, but the monitor rejected requests for numeric data. The scope field, which specifies the range of a query, had been written as 2 bytes instead of the required 4 bytes. This was corrected.

Numeric request format before and after the fix · MX850, August 13

code 10		Invalid request argument

Numeric readings received00

The monitor returned a different error after the change, but no numeric readings were received. A later reconnection attempt also received no response, and the test was ended.

Two-way communication through the cable was confirmed. Work on the numeric request settings continued in the next monitor test.

September 18, 2026 · MX750 DEMO mode

Receiving and decoding MX750 readings

This test used the RS232 port on the MX750’s rear connector board. Pins 2 and 3 of the existing DB9 cable were swapped to match this port.

Network settings were also checked. DHCP was selected in Network Status, and the IP address, subnet and gateway were all 0.0.0.0. The final connection used RS232 serial communication, which does not require an IP address.

The optional MIB port used on the MX850 and the MX750 connector-board port had different transmit and receive wiring. DB9 pin 2 was changed to white/brown and pin 3 to white/blue, while pin 5 remained ground.

The initial test received no response. After the Mac set the baud rate, the port closed and the USB–RS232 adapter reverted to 9600 baud. When the transmitter and receiver use different rates, their bit timing no longer matches, so valid requests and responses cannot be decoded.

Responses arrived after the port was opened and kept open while setting 115200 baud to match the monitor. The numeric request length, one-second polling interval and value decoding were then corrected.

18:02 KST · About 16 seconds · MX750 DEMO responses

September 21, 2026 · Biomedical engineering bench test

MX800 screen capture and numeric data

The MX800 was connected to a Mac with the biomedical engineering team. The monitor’s video output was received through a capture card, while numeric data arrived through MIB/RS232 and a USB–RS232 adapter.

Two input paths from the MX800
PathInputDisplay
VideoMonitor video output → Elgato → MacThe full monitor screen, including readings and waveforms
Numeric dataMIB/RS232 → USB–RS232 → MacDecoded readings displayed separately on Mac and XR

At 405 seconds, 843 Poll Results totaling 187,544 bytes had been received, with 0 CRC or parser errors. The connection aborted 6 times and automatically reconnected all 6 times.

Image orientation was compared between Photo Booth and direct capture. Photo Booth showed a mirrored image, while AVFoundation capture at 1920×1080 UYVY and the Mac app showed the correct orientation.

The readings received on the Mac were sent to the XR emulator. It displayed HR, SpO₂, RR and trends for the past 60 seconds. At this stage, those trends used numeric data arriving at approximately 1 Hz.

September 30, 2026 · Generated signals / emulator

Adding waveforms and fixing display flicker

Alongside the readings received once per second, processing was added for ECG samples at 500 Hz, Pleth at 125 Hz and Resp at 62.5 Hz. During tests with generated signals, all three waveforms briefly disappeared together while the numbers remained visible.

Two consecutive frames from the September 30 emulator recording · Generated signals

Subtracting the new data’s arrival time from the previous display-update time briefly produced a negative age. This was incorrectly treated as “no signal.” Negative ages were clamped to 0, and the waveforms were changed to sweep across a fixed display area.

October 1, 2026 · Generated DEMO / emulator

Compact readings over the video

A compact overlay was added for HR, SpO₂ and RR. Generated DEMO signals were used to test the readings and the overlay’s position and size controls.

The overlay’s on/off control was placed in the vital signs panel.

ECG, Pleth and Resp waveforms were also added to a separate vital signs panel and played back using generated DEMO input.

2026.10.07–08

Internal alpha and Mac Studio setup

Builds were uploaded for internal TestFlight alpha testing: 0.2.0(7) on October 7 and 0.2.1(9) the next day.

The app was installed on the new Mac Studio and opened to the connection screen. The previously separate vital signs receiver was integrated into the Mac app, and its communication and decoding results were compared with the original program. On October 8, Galaxy XR was switched to receive vital signs from the Studio, and the displayed readings were checked.

2026.10.14

Preparing the equipment cart for the operating room

A monitor, keyboard and mouse were arranged on a mobile cart for using the new Mac Studio in the operating room.

2026.10.15

Video, vital signs and CT in the operating room

During the operating room test, Galaxy XR displayed endoscopic video, a vital sign waveform panel and a CT slice together. A compact readings overlay appeared at the bottom of the video.

October 15–17, 2026 · Playback comparison and release-build testing

Steady playback when waveform data arrives in bursts

After the operating room test, waveform playback was found to stop and start. Packets containing 256 ms of data arrived in bursts of four, with gaps of up to 892 ms before the next burst. The display drew all the data it had received, then waited for the next packet.

The playback buffer was increased from 256 ms to 1.024 seconds to hold four packets. Both Mac and XR were updated to advance by sample time and continue drawing buffered data between packet arrivals.

14.8-second synthetic waveform test using 60 recorded packet-arrival intervals
ConditionPlayback-clock stalls / Checks
Before317 / 925
After0 / 925

Buffering adds approximately 1 second of display delay. The comparison above tests playback behavior using recorded packet-arrival intervals.

October 15, 2026 · Diagnosis and fix

Why the ECG had gaps and white markers

On October 15, dense white markers appeared over the ECG in Galaxy XR. On the Mac, the ECG trace looked like a dashed line.

Analysis showed that some bits representing sample amplitude were being misread as invalid-value flags or pacemaker markers.

The decoder was changed to check the complete status-bit pattern. Valid samples are drawn as waveforms, while actual missing data and special signals retain their indicators.
